classification.difficultyReason: Subtract two bearings from one lighthouse and use cosine rule for ship separation.

content.prompt:
In the diagram shown, ship $A$ is 120 nautical miles from lighthouse $L$ on a bearing of $072^\circ\mathrm{T}$, while ship $B$ is 180 nautical miles from $L$ on a bearing of $136^\circ\mathrm{T}$.
Calculate the distance between the two ships, correct to the nearest nautical mile.

spec.description: Black triangle with L upper left, A upper right and B lower right. Dashed north arrow at L, overlapping turquoise bearing sector, 72° above L and 136° below-left with a curved leader. The 120 Nm label has a curved leader to LA; 180 Nm is outside LB. AB is unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: LA=120 nautical miles, LB=180 nautical miles; bearings from L are 072° and 136°. No requested distance or derived included angle appears.
